item.name: 0. OAuth2 Login (PKCE)
item.description: Drives the real Authorization Code + PKCE flow against a running auth-service, the same sequence raitukashtam-web/mobile clients use (and the same one this repo's own PkceFlowClient test helper exercises). Run these 4 requests IN ORDER, top to bottom, with a fresh Postman run each time (state is chained via collection variables). After step 4 succeeds, {{bearerToken}} is populated and every other request in this collection (they already use Bearer {{bearerToken}} auth) will work.

request.description: Establishes the 'saved request' in the session Spring Security will redirect back to after login. Postman's cookie jar automatically keeps the SESSION cookie for the next requests -- nothing to do manually here.

Only works if step 1 ran first in the same Postman session (needs the SESSION cookie + saved request). If reCAPTCHA kicks in (repeated failed attempts), add a 'recaptchaToken' form field -- see LoginAttemptService.

item.name: Verify an OTP and authenticate the browser/app session

request.name: Verify an OTP and authenticate the browser/app session

description.content: Public, unauthenticated, rate-limited (10/hour/IP). Finds or creates the Identity/User behind this mobile number (linking to an existing account registered under it via another method, e.g. password, if one exists -- otherwise provisioning a brand-new phone-only account), ensures a MyCommunity product membership (this is mycommunity's own login path, kept separate from the generic default RAITUKASHTAM product other self-service flows use), and establishes an authenticated session, the same way /google/verify-token does for Google sign-in. The client then continues with the same /oauth2/authorize (Authorization Code + PKCE) request against the mycommunity-android client -- with the session now authenticated, that proceeds straight to issuing a code instead of redirecting to /login.

item.name: Verify a Google ID token and authenticate the browser session

request.name: Verify a Google ID token and authenticate the browser session

description.content: Public, unauthenticated -- called by the frontend with a real Google ID token obtained via Google Identity Services. On success, creates/links an Identity and establishes an authenticated session; the frontend then continues with the same /oauth2/authorize request it already uses for password login.
Public, unauthenticated, rate-limited (5/hour/IP). Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists, to avoid leaking account existence.

info.name: auth-service (local)
info.description: Generated from the live OpenAPI spec (GET /v3/api-docs) of the auth-service container running locally at {{baseUrl}}. Folder '0. OAuth2 Login (PKCE)' drives the real Authorization Code + PKCE flow (run in order once) to populate {{bearerToken}}, which every other request in this collection already uses via Bearer auth. Native Spring Authorization Server endpoints (/oauth2/authorize, /login, /oauth2/token, /oauth2/jwks) aren't in the app's own OpenAPI spec (no Swagger annotations on framework-provided routes), so folder 0 was added by hand -- everything else here is auto-generated from the live spec, not hand-written.
